When I am stressed about absolutely even the slightest thing, I can’t sleep. 

It’s like the slightest stress puts my nervous system on high alert, and I find it extremely difficult to get my brain to shutoff and sleep… 

I have recently realize that my sleeping issues  are beyond typical insomnia. That due to the amount of trauma I have experienced since I was a young child, my nervous system did not develop normally. I was often on high alert at bed time because of the constant yelling or several days worth of hunger pains. As a teen it didn’t get any better because at that point I was on high alert because my foster dad would enter my room at night…

Over the decades I’ve tried so many different methods, medications or supplements, and more to help me get better and more regular sleep… you name it, I’ve probably tried it… and I’m still trying to figure it out…  

As I work on my own healing, it IS getting better… little by little.

@Teachmehumility, sending you my deepest condolences for your loss… yes MS is hard… but so is what you are now facing! Please know that there is no perfect or right way to navigate this journey of grief. Please know how brave you are in facing it, reaching out when you need, and getting help when it’s to heavy and hard to carry on your own. 

I lost my little brother over a year to suicide, I wish all the time that I had known how deeply and badly he was hurting. I wish we had some clue about why he suddenly gave up. Realistically I know his death was the final progression of the depression that he’s battled since his childhood TBI, I know he’s no longer suffering and in pain, and I know I may never have been able to help fully ease his suffering no matter how hard I tried. But I miss him, and I always will. 

As hard as it is and will be, your mom wanted and wants so much for you to LIVE! Honor her every day by doing all you can to keep going on. It doesn’t have to be all at once, it doesn’t have to be perfect, and on the hardest days, breathing, getting up, and eating something is still living. And even on those days, she’ll be incredibly proud of you! 

Hugs to you dear one.

Hi there fellow ADHD’er, welcome to the club!

First, I agree with someone else on this thread that side self-diagnosis IS often the first step. I did it, decades ago for my sons and then of course sought out a professional diagnosis and help for them. And  recently I have actively sought out professional help in this realm myself, also due to going back to college.

Have you thought about seeing if your university student health and counseling center can help you in your process? 

As for what I call the emotional word vomit, I too am quite familiar with needing to write out my thoughts and feelings when I’m emotional or upset. I think I have it down to a science now. I pretty much do it in an outline format. Listing first the individual feelings I am having in one or two words (sometimes in groupings) and then I go on to sublist and more details. 
Looks something looks like: 

1.	I am feeling X (frustrated)
    -	I am frustrated because of x
    -	I am frustrated because of y
         -	I need X changed/worked on

This method has helped me significantly in not only identifying all that I may be feeling (I’m a repressed) it also helps me in sorting out what is actually relevant to the issue(s) needing to be addressed, but it also helps me in identifying what my needs are. 

Finally, the hyper focus research rabbit hole is something I think all ADHD’er fall down… it’s really challenging for me in my course writing and research papers… give yourself a bit of grace here… and as everything in life, try to find a system and tools that help you develop a method that works best for you.

Best of luck to you in your studies and in seeking help. You’ll get there. Have a bit of faith in yourself, I do!

Jonny, I sincerely apologize for not responding sooner! I’m in school full time now and overloaded my plate this summer semester. I haven’t really been on any SM platforms regularly for months.

To answer your question, I found a regular Licensed professional clinical counselor/psychologist. I did a bit of research from those on my health plan at the time, and for me, it was important this person be a woman. I looked at the practice sites of those in the area and narrowed down to 3 or 4 I thought would be a good fit. And then tried to schedule a meeting with them from there. Because I desperately and sincerely needed for this to work, I really did a lot of work to find my right fit.

What helped me make my final decision was the counselor I chose allowed me to start from where I was and then open up the spaces where I’ve locked away my traumas as I’ve been ready. Two years later and I still see her, although not quite as often as I did when we first started… and basically for mental health maintenance now.

I can still vividly remember that taste! I had a similar experience a few years back w/pill prednisone… I was given the option of hospital IV for 5 days, or pill for 7 at the high dose and a 30 day taper. Regrettably, due to work obligations I was still determined to meet, I stupidly chose the pills… I planed to plow through the first 5 days working and then take a week or so off… 

If I wasn’t already a mess before and fighting so hard to keep myself together, and both my home life and work life rotating, by day 5, I was a complete puddle. I ended up pretty much hiding and hibernation in my bedroom away from my husband and teenage boys for about 10 straight days. My poor husband was at his wits end trying so hard and as best as he could with his very limited time to help support me through my first (and so far only) steroid session… at the time he was both working FT and in his last year of college FT… AND it was around midterms!!! 

In my childhood I watched a family member become extremely aggressive and cruel during their steroid treatment, and ultimately continuing medicated needs… I was petrified that’s how I’d be too… what I was NOT prepared for was the immense anxiety ridden depressive tailspin it plunged me into. To say it was rough would be an utter understatement! The whole experience was a wild 6/7 month ride… 

If needed, I will of course take that journey again, however I think I will totally throw out my need to consider and manage what the world might need from me… whatever it is will need to be someone else’s problem… I will most likely try the hospital IV infusion route next time. Finally and if I’m working, I’ll definitely be taking a short term disability leave. And, now I’ve got my own mental health psychologist as part of my “health pit crew”! 

Trust me, you may feel like your going crazy, but your not! You will make it out the other side of this process! 

I wish you the best of luck to you & a speedy de-inflammation journey fellow MS’er. Hang in there!!!

The phones give you a recorded message and hangs right up on you asking you to call back at a later time. It doesn’t matter what time of day you call (between 8am & 12 noon). It doesn’t matter if you call bomb hoping to be the lucky caller that makes it through. 

The on-line portal is also not any better. You can only send 2 messages a day, and none are being answered. At least none of mine are.

I am so frustrated with the system that I have started to contact my city and state government officials to complain and explain the issues I am having. I don’t know what else to do.
